pairs.difference: A: the anchor's flukes are crude flat triangles stuck onto a thick rubbery crown. The stock is a short block clamped on with an oversized collar, and the ring is fat compared with the thin shank, so the parts don't connect the way a real anchor's do. B: the barrel has a believable bulge and its four hoops are thin, evenly spaced bands. Its silhouette is very solid (0.985), but that suits a barrel.
pairs.fix: Draw an iron anchor with a long straight shank, a thin round ring at the top and a straight wooden stock at full width. Give the two curved arms a narrow crown and small spade-shaped flukes that grow out of the arms, with no added clamp collar.

pairs.difference: A: the coin sack is a soft round sack with a ruffled neck. A soft object should look puffy, and the coins are flat disks. B: the vending machine is a crisp box with flat panels, straight sides, tight corners and small feet. Both have believable proportions.

B: the galleon's hull is short and toy-like under an oversized stack of sails. The sails float on spars with no clear mast lines. The bowsprit is a stubby pipe jutting from the side, and the masts overlap in a jumble, so the parts are miscounted and badly connected. A: the rowboat has a long, believable hull with flat thwart boards. The dock planks and post are straight, and the cropped framing matches the real cards.
pairs.fix: Draw a sailing ship with a long, low hull and three clearly separate upright masts. Each mast carries sails hung from thin straight yards. Run a thin bowsprit straight out from the bow at the front. Keep the sails in proportion to the hull.

pairs.difference: A: the snorkel tube is a thick sausage that loops around the mask. The mouthpiece is a swollen blob, and the mask's rim and skirt are inflated so much that the silhouette has almost no corners (corner_rate 1.08, below the real range). B: the slide's ladder rails and rungs are thin and straight, the support posts are straight, and the platform is a flat slab.
pairs.fix: Draw a dive mask with a slim, firm frame around a flat glass lens and a thin rubber strap. Attach a slender, straight snorkel tube to the strap with a small clip, with only a gentle bend at the bottom into a small mouthpiece.

pairs.difference: A: the map sheet has a thick, raised, rolled border and gently swollen waves along its edges, so it reads as a padded mat rather than paper (straight_share 0.742, above the real range). B: the map is a thin sheet with straight fold creases and sharp corners. The magnifier's ring and handle are in proportion.
pairs.fix: Draw the map as a thin sheet of paper lying flat, with crisp straight edges, sharp corners and a few fold creases. Don't give it a raised or puffy border.

pairs.difference: B: the spiral topiary is drawn as a stack of separate swollen balls rather than one continuous spiral cut around a cone. The tiers bulge outward, and the base ring is a puffy disk. A: the palm has a believable curved trunk, separate fronds with notched edges, and coconuts in proportion.
pairs.fix: Draw a cone-shaped topiary with a single continuous spiral groove winding up it, with clipped tiers tapering evenly to a point. Set it in a low, flat-edged stone planter ring.

pairs.difference: A: the coin-operated viewer's head is a swollen, pillowy capsule. The lenses are tiny compared with the bulk of the head, the side handle is a thick loop, and the post collar is bloated. B: the ship's wheel has a thin round rim, eight even spokes, turned handles and a straight post on a flat base plate.
pairs.fix: Draw a sightseeing binocular viewer with a boxy metal head with flat sides and two large round eyepieces. Mount it on a slim neck over a straight pole, with thin side handles.

pairs.difference: B: the bell buoy is built from stacked fat cylinders. The frame holding the bell is one thick sausage loop instead of a thin open lattice of rails, so the thin parts have been thickened. A: the instant photo is a flat, crisp rectangle with straight edges and sharp corners.
pairs.fix: Draw a navigation buoy with a flat float at the waterline and a slim tapering body. On top, add an open cage of thin metal rods holding a small bell.

pairs.difference: A: the parrot's body is short and compressed between oversized wings. The wings join the body at odd points, and the edge is broken into many small jags (corner_rate 9.8, far above the real range). B: the balloons are simple ovals, and the thin strings and small knots are kept thin.
pairs.fix: Draw a macaw in flight with a long body and head in proportion. Both wings attach at the shoulders and spread evenly, with a long, narrow tail behind.

pairs.difference: A: the tricorn's brim is a fat rolled tube with blobby upturned ends, and the crown is a swollen dome. It reads as an inflated two-cornered hat rather than a three-cornered one with stiff folded brims. B: the jacket is soft and puffy, but cloth is allowed to be. The collar, pockets and cuffs are all present and in the right places.
pairs.fix: Draw a three-cornered hat with a thin, stiff brim turned up in three flat sides that meet at three sharp points, over a low crown.

pairs.difference: A: the spyglass's telescoping sections are swollen round sausages with no crisp step between them. The silhouette has no corners at all (corner_rate 0.0, below the real range). B: the oil lamp has a believable glass chimney, a flat base foot and a thin handle loop.
pairs.fix: Draw a brass spyglass made of straight cylinders that step down in width. Give each section a flat edge where it meets the next, a thin rim at the eyepiece and a wider rim at the lens end.

pairs.difference: A: the chest's lid is a bulging dome, and the gold bands and corner caps are thick rounded blobs. The box faces swell outward, and the corners are soft. B: the chest has flat plank faces, straight edges and tight, crisp corners. The metal trim is thin and even.
pairs.fix: Draw a treasure chest as a box with flat wooden faces and straight edges. Edge it with thin metal strips and small square corner caps. Give it an open lid with a gentle, even curve.

pattern: Generated cards inflate the object: thin parts become thick tubes (snorkel tube, buoy frame, hat brim, spyglass sections, chest bands), flat boxes and sheets get swollen faces and blobby corners, and the parts are miscounted or badly connected (the galleon's masts and bowsprit, the anchor's flukes, the topiary built from stacked balls).
